summary: Palm Springs International Airport serves the popular desert resort destination of Palm Springs in California's Coachella Valley. Originally established as a military training facility during World War II, it has evolved into a key gateway for tourists visiting the greater Palm Springs area. The airport hosts the famous annual Palm Springs International Film Festival and offers travelers immediate access to the region's renowned golf courses, spas, and outdoor recreation.
faqs:
Q: How far is Palm Springs International Airport from downtown Palm Springs?
A: The airport is conveniently located just about 2 miles (3 km) east of downtown Palm Springs, making it one of the most accessible airports in Southern California.

Q: Does Palm Springs International Airport have a single terminal?
A: Yes, PSP operates from one main terminal building with two concourses, which makes navigation simple and quick for travelers.

Q: Which airlines serve Palm Springs International Airport?
A: Major carriers including American, Delta, United, Southwest, Alaska, and several seasonal airlines operate flights to PSP from cities across North America.

Q: Is Palm Springs International Airport busy year-round?
A: Traffic peaks during winter months when snowbirds and tourists flock to the warm desert climate, while summer tends to be quieter.
transport_tips: The airport is just a short drive from downtown Palm Springs, typically under 10 minutes by car or rideshare. Taxis, Uber, and Lyft are readily available outside the terminal, and rental car counters are located on-site for visitors planning to explore the broader Coachella Valley. Many area hotels also offer complimentary shuttle services, so check with your accommodation before arrival.
local_tip: For a uniquely Palm Springs experience, time your visit during the winter months to enjoy perfect 70°F weather and avoid the intense summer heat, and don't miss the airport's outdoor observation area where you can watch planes arrive against the stunning San Jacinto mountain backdrop.
